lesson.menu_title: Advanced Speaking -- The Panel: Adding Context Without Losing the Room
lesson.menu_desc: Carlos is on stage at an M&A integration forum. Build on other panelists, chime in without digressing, tell a short anecdote, and add context in the middle of a sentence with non-defining relative clauses -- "Tom, who runs finance at Brightline, saw the first warning"
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 27 -- Advanced Speaking -- The Panel: Adding Context Without Losing the Room
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Carlos Vinicius Vale Bassan | Lesson 27 -- The Panel
lesson.grammar_point: non-defining relative clauses (, who / , which / , where; which for a whole idea)

listenings.text: I have moderated more than two hundred panels, and the best panelists all do three things. First, they listen. They build on what the last speaker said, so the panel sounds like a conversation, not four separate speeches. Second, they keep it short. If you want to chime in, take thirty seconds, not three minutes, and never digress into a story that has no point. Third, they give the audience something concrete. A short anecdote or a case in point is worth more than ten slides. And here is a small trick for adding context. Put the extra information in the middle of your sentence, between commas. For example: our client, which is a family business, had never done a deal before. The audience gets the context, and you never lose your main point.

Good afternoon, everyone. My name is Daniel Ortiz, and I lead integration at Kestrel Partners, which invests in mid-size logistics companies. I want to start with a confession. Our first acquisition, which was in two thousand nineteen, almost failed. We had a great strategy, but we forgot about people. The CEO of the company we bought, who had built it from nothing, left after three months, and half of his team followed him. Today we do it differently. Before we sign, we spend a full week in the company, where we meet everyone from the drivers to the board. It sounds slow, which it is, but it saves us months later. I am happy to build on this in the Q&A.
